headline: MGAT Alpha closed 13 trades this week for a net -$93.65 (15.38% win rate, 2 of 13) -- every family lost, and without two take-profits worth $35.76 combined the week would have been -$129.41. The book is still ahead of its own hold-and-never-trade benchmark since launch (+3.00% against -14.75% for holding the same seven coins untouched), but that gap widened because the comparison basket fell harder, not because the book gained -- the book itself lost money this week too. The run since the latest restart (segment 2) has now crossed the pre-set 50-close checkpoint at 53 closes with one family's win rate at 20.69%, which is why this week's call is 'needs a change' rather than 'needs improvement'.

counterfactual.reason: The shadow comparison book is void for this run: it could never close a position, so none of its figures measure anything.

hold_benchmark.basis: $8,000 split equally across the seven coins the book bought in its first two cycles on 2026-08-25, held untouched, no fees

llm_adviser: LLM adviser: observer only — logs what it would do, cannot affect a trade (settled from source 2026-09-22).
sample_caveat: 13 closed trades this week, 128 all-time against the 200-trade target (64%). All-time is past the floor where win rate and PnL become directional rather than unreadable. The current run (segment 2) is now 53 closes, past the 50-close checkpoint set after the prior week's report; its 18.87% win rate is a second meaningful read, still directional rather than conclusive.
paper_caveat: Alpha is paper — simulated fills, no slippage, no thin-liquidity exits, no can't-sell-into-dust. A clean logic result here is never a claim that the execution floor works; that claim belongs to the Beta rung alone.
integrity: No CLASS-A changes landed in this week's window — the latest health-log entry is dated before it — so the comparison with the previous week is clean.

verdict.text: Needs a change. The checkpoint set two weeks ago has now tripped: the current run (segment 2) is at 53 closes, past the 50-close mark, with one family's win rate at 20.69% (6 of 29, -$184.63), under the roughly 25% bar used as the trigger. Every family lost this week -- 13 closes, 2 wins, -$93.65 (-1.12% of book); without the two take-profits the week would have been -$129.41, and 9 of 13 exits were stop-losses. Re-buying back into a family shortly after a stop happened more than once this week and looks like it is adding to the losses, though that is unverified from this read alone. Sizing is not the problem: 90% of opens used measured betas, and the measured-beta trades are where most of the loss sits. Against the hold benchmark the book is still ahead -- about 11 points even with one early outsized print excluded -- but the comparison basket fell harder than the book did; the book itself lost money this week, so that gap is damage limitation, not an edge. No faults worth separating out: one transient witness-fetch failure and clean time-stops.
